resale_co.name: Certificate of Inspection (Residential Real Estate Inspection), also listed in the fee schedule as a Certificate for resale
resale_co.issued_by: Borough of Ridgefield Building Department (Construction Official or designee)
resale_co.lead_time: By code, the Construction Official inspects within five days of the application and issues or denies the certificate within 10 days. Violations must be corrected within 14 days, with a reinspection within 14 days.
resale_co.valid_for: A temporary certificate of inspection (for repairs that do not affect safety or habitability) expires 60 days after issuance.
requirements: Inspection showing the home and its intended use comply with Borough and State building, zoning, health, safety and fire codes
Smoke and carbon monoxide Certificate of Compliance, also issued by the Building Department / Construction Official
Carbon monoxide sensor device in each dwelling unit with a fuel-burning source (Borough Chapter 146 applies to newly sold homes)
Correct any violations within 14 days of the notice

fees.label: Certificate of inspection, one-family (Code Section 390-264)
fees.quote: The fee for the certificate of inspection as provided for herein shall be $125 for one-family, $250 for two-family, $250 for the first two units in multifamily dwellings and $50 for each additional unit

fees.label: Certificate of inspection, two-family (Code Section 390-264)
fees.quote: The fee for the certificate of inspection as provided for herein shall be $125 for one-family, $250 for two-family, $250 for the first two units in multifamily dwellings and $50 for each additional unit

fees.label: Certificate of inspection reinspection after violations (Code Section 390-264)
fees.quote: there shall be due from the owner or his authorized representative an additional fee of $50 for each such reinspection.

fees.label: Zoning certificate for resale of a one-family (Chapter 140 fee schedule)
fees.quote: Certificate for resale of a one-family$150

fees.label: Zoning certificate for resale of a two-family (Chapter 140 fee schedule)
fees.quote: Certificate for resale of a two-family$250

fees.label: Resale or rental reinspection (Chapter 140 zoning fee schedule)

resale_co.how_to_apply: Apply in writing to the Building Department, 700 Shaler Boulevard, Ridgefield, NJ 07657 (Monday to Friday 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., no financial transactions after 3:00 p.m.), paying the fee with the application. The Borough website does not post the application form; call (201) 943-5546 or email the Construction Official to get it. Zoning appointments are Tuesday and Thursday after 4:00 p.m. (email jsetticase@ridgefieldboro.com).

evidence.quote: No person shall convey or transfer title or ownership to any residential real property within the Borough of Ridgefield, nor shall any person accept conveyance or transfer of title to residential real property, unless and until a certificate of inspection is issued in accordance with this article.
evidence.doc_date: Ord. No. 2208 (9-10-2012); fee amended 5-28-2024 by Ord. No. 2488

evidence.quote: The certificate shall be issued or denied within 10 days of the date of application to the Building Department.
Said temporary certificate shall automatically expire 60 days after its issuance.
All newly sold homes where a continuing certificate of occupancy is required.

resale_co.notes: Ridgefield Code Part 15, Residential Real Estate Inspection (Sections 390-260 to 390-271), was read through the ecode360 print view. The Chapter 140 Building Construction fee schedule separately lists zoning fees for a 'Certificate for resale' of $150 (one-family) and $250 (two-family), plus $75 per resale reinspection, while Section 390-264 (amended May 2024) sets the certificate of inspection at $125 and $250. It is not clear whether both are charged on a sale or whether the Chapter 140 figures replaced the older ones; ask the Building Department. The Borough website (ridgefieldnj.gov; the old ridgefieldboro.com redirects there) does not post a resale form or resale fee. Rental registration, rent leveling and lead-based paint inspections (Part 16) are rental programs.

requirements: Smoke detectors on every level of the dwelling, including basements, and outside each sleeping area
Carbon monoxide detectors in the immediate vicinity of sleeping areas, unless the home has no fuel-burning appliance and no attached garage

authorities.name: Borough of Ridgefield Building Department (Construction Official); the Fire Prevention Bureau does not issue these certificates
authorities.how_to_apply: Contact the Building Department at (201) 943-5546 or gyfantis@ridgefieldboro.com; the Borough page says the Building Department and Construction Official issue the smoke and carbon monoxide Certificate of Compliance for a transfer of ownership.

evidence.quote: A Certificate of Compliance for smoke and carbon monoxide detectors is required for the transfer of ownership of a dwelling.
Certificates are issued by the Building Department and the Construction Official.
The Fire Prevention Bureau does not issue these certificates.

LEAID: 0249-001 Ridgefield Boro SMOKE DETECTOR COMPLIANCE Name: Ridgefield Boro Bldg Dept Enf Auth. Municipal Addr: 550 Edison St. Fire Official John J Hoffman Phone (201) 943-5546 Email jhoffman@ridgefieldboro.com

fire_cert.notes: The NJ DCA fire directory also lists the Ridgefield Building Department (phone (201) 943-5546) as the smoke detector compliance office, with John J Hoffman as Fire Official of the Fire Prevention Bureau (550 Edison Street, (201) 945-6008). No fee for the smoke/CO certificate is published by the Borough. Code Section 146-6 sets a $5 carbon monoxide detector inspection fee 'unless a contrary fee is established by the Department of Community Affairs', which is outdated and not used as a fee here. The Fire Prevention Bureau's free Smoke Detector Program is a resident service, not the sale certificate.

other_items.label: Zoning resale certificate fee
other_items.detail: The Chapter 140 fee schedule lists zoning fees for a certificate for resale ($150 one-family, $250 two-family, $75 reinspection); confirm whether this is a separate zoning review from the certificate of inspection.

open_questions: Is the resale fee $125/$250 (Section 390-264) or $150/$250 (Chapter 140 zoning schedule), or are both charged?
What is the fee and lead time for the smoke/CO Certificate of Compliance issued by the Building Department?
Where is the application form for the certificate of inspection (not posted online)?
Is a fire extinguisher still required at resale after P.L.2025, c.19?
